exposure: Mode of delivery (elective cesarean vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery)
outcome: Absolute counts and percentages of peripheral blood T-cell subsets (maturation and activation profiles)
finding: Women who underwent spontaneous vaginal delivery had significantly lower absolute counts of B cells and natural killer-like T (NKT-like) cells in peripheral blood compared to those who had elective cesareans, but no other significant differences in T-cell subsets or regulatory T and B cells were observed.
mod_finding: This study found that women who had spontaneous vaginal deliveries had significantly lower absolute counts of B cells and natural killer-like T cells in their peripheral blood compared to women who had elective cesareans.
